cues.en: So template variables
are another very important
component and template-related feature offered by Angular.
And you can really become creative with them.
For example, we don't have to provide
the entire object as an input to onSubmit
if we actually only care about the title in there.
We could change onSubmit and expect to get the title,
which should be of type string,
and the ticketText, which should be of type string.
And then we could just log the title here
and also log the ticketText.
Now, of course, we would have to change the template,
because currently, I'm passing the entire
DOM object and not just a title.
But of course, since title input
is that underlying input element object,
we can also access .value here,
and therefore, pass just the entered value
to onSubmit when the form is submitted.
And to also get the text
that was entered into the text area,
we can also add a template variable to that text area
and get the text input and submit that
as a second argument to onSubmit.
And now, we would do the extraction work
here in the template and get the extracted values
in the component method
and in the component class, therefore.
And that is simply an alternative way
of using those template variables.
With that approach, of course if I enter something here
and I click Submit, I do get those values.
So that works the way you would expect it to work.
So we explored template variables
and how you, for example, can use them
to extract input values when the form is submitted
as we're doing it here.
But of course you can use them
and the access to dom elements they give you
in any way you need.
What's worth noting about these template variables
is that they don't always give you access
to the dom element though.
Here with title input it is the HTML input element
we're getting access to.
And for the text input here,
it's the HTML text area element.

maybe called BTN, then the type of value
that's stored in that variable is button component,
not HTML button element.
The latter would be the case
if I would not have this app button attribute on the button,
which turns this into an instance of my button component.
Without it, it's not,
and then indeed it is a HTML button element
that's stored in that variable.
But if I add that attribute,
Angular takes over control of that button and in the end,
turns it into an instance of my button component

And if that's the case, if you are dealing with an instance
of a component you defined

on that element in your template,
so on that component element like here on this button,
then it's actually that component instance
